symbols.name: number of axes
symbols.meaning: The number of cyclic axes, which is the number of pairwise coprime axis lengths.
symbols.quote: There are $D$ cyclic axes, and axis $i$ has $\lambda_i$ positions.

symbols.name: axis length
symbols.meaning: The number of positions on axis $i$, the number of values its coordinate takes.
symbols.quote: There are $D$ cyclic axes, and axis $i$ has $\lambda_i$ positions.

symbols.name: generator indeterminate
symbols.meaning: A formal symbol, never evaluated, whose powers index the positions of the one-dimensional ring.
symbols.quote: Let $x$ be an indeterminate, a formal symbol that is never evaluated, whose powers index positions.

symbols.name: axis indeterminate
symbols.meaning: The indeterminate of axis $i$ in the multidimensional ring.
symbols.quote: where $x_i$ is the indeterminate of axis $i$ (the letter $x_i$ changes meaning from earlier pages).

symbols.name: axis exponent
symbols.meaning: The exponent of $x_i$ in a monomial of the multidimensional ring.
symbols.quote: Its monomials $x_1^{\eta_1}\cdots x_D^{\eta_D}$ have $\eta_i$ as the exponent of $x_i$.

symbols.name: power exponent
symbols.quote:
For an integer $
u\ge 0$ (the exponent of $\Phi(x)$; the letter $
u$ changes meaning from earlier pages), $\Phi(x)^
u=\prod_i x_i^{\mu_i
u}$ equals $1$ exactly when $\lambda_i\mid
u$ for every $i$.

symbols.name: coefficient index
symbols.meaning: An ordinary coefficient index in $[0,\Lambda)$, the position of a coefficient in the one-dimensional ring.
symbols.quote: Let $e$ be an ordinary coefficient index, $0\le e<\Lambda$ (the letter $e$ changes meaning from earlier pages).

symbols.name: first exponent
symbols.meaning: The smaller of two exponents of $\Phi(x)$ compared for equality, an integer with $0\le a<\Lambda$.
symbols.quote: suppose $\Phi(x)^a=\Phi(x)^b$ for exponents $a$ and $b$ with $0\le a<b<\Lambda$.

symbols.name: second exponent
symbols.meaning: The larger of two exponents of $\Phi(x)$ compared for equality, an integer with $a<b<\Lambda$.
symbols.quote: suppose $\Phi(x)^a=\Phi(x)^b$ for exponents $a$ and $b$ with $0\le a<b<\Lambda$.

symbols.name: axis coordinate
symbols.meaning: The coordinate of the index $e$ on axis $i$, an integer in $[0,\lambda_i)$.
symbols.quote: Let $\gamma_i\in[0,\lambda_i)$ be the coordinate of $e$ on axis $i$, meaning the exponent of $x_i$ in $\Phi(x^e)$ reduced modulo $\lambda_i$.

symbols.name: exponent
symbols.meaning: A nonnegative integer exponent of $x_i$, the power to which the indeterminate of axis $i$ is raised.
symbols.quote: Indeed, for an integer $k\ge 0$ (an exponent of $x_i$), $x_i^k=1$ exactly when $\lambda_i\mid k$, because reducing $k$ modulo $\lambda_i$ leaves one of the distinct basis monomials $x_i^0,\dots,x_i^{\lambda_i-1}$, and only $x_i^0=1$ equals $1$.

symbols.name: row index
symbols.meaning: The row index of the transform matrix $A_i$, running from $0$ to $\lambda_i-1$.
symbols.quote: Let $\sigma$ be the row index and $\eta$ the column index, both running from $0$ to $\lambda_i-1$, and let $A_i$ be the $\lambda_i\times\lambda_i$ matrix with entry $\omega_i^{\sigma\eta}$ in row $\sigma$ and column $\eta$.

symbols.name: axis transform matrix
symbols.meaning: The $\lambda_i\times\lambda_i$ matrix with entry $\omega_i^{\sigma\eta}$ in row $\sigma$ and column $\eta$, the transform on axis $i$.
symbols.quote: Let $\omega_i$ be a primitive $\lambda_i$-th root of unity. Let $\sigma$ be the row index and $\eta$ the column index, both running from $0$ to $\lambda_i-1$, and let $A_i$ be the $\lambda_i\times\lambda_i$ matrix with entry $\omega_i^{\sigma\eta}$ in row $\sigma$ and column $\eta$.

symbols.name: Kronecker product
symbols.meaning: The Kronecker (tensor) product of matrices, which combines the one-axis transforms into a transform on all axes.
symbols.quote: The symbol $\otimes$ denotes the Kronecker (tensor) product of matrices, so $A_1\otimes\cdots\otimes A_D$ applies $A_i$ along axis $i$ alone.

relations.quote: It is applied to a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) and turns it into a multidimensional cyclic convolution whose axes have pairwise [coprime](coprime.md) lengths.
It places the coefficients of a [radix-digit convolution](radix-digit-convolution.md) on distinct prime cyclic axes.
The Chinese-remainder map computes its coordinates from the mixed-radix digits of $e$.
